title: Eta Aquilae: TESS sector 81 light curve (a classical Cepheid)
credit: TESS, sector 81 (NASA; SPOC light curve from MAST)

license.statement: NASA mission data, released through MAST without restriction on reuse. MAST asks that work using its data acknowledge the mission and the archive.

columns.name: flux error
columns.description: propagated PDCSAP error over the median, one sigma, per bin

masks.rule: any nonzero flag drops the cadence
a bin with fewer than 3 kept cadences is dropped

reductions: 60-minute bins average 30 two-minute cadences each; the bin error is the quadrature sum over the count.
Flux is stored to 20 ppm, its error to 1 ppm and time to 0.0001 d (8.6 s); the manifest records the largest rounding.

Eta Aql is a naked-eye star (Tmag 3.1), saturated in TESS: the SPOC aperture collects the bleed trails and the light curve carries systematics at the few-percent level, which is why the residuals about a Fourier fit are larger than the photon noise. The run covers about 3.7 cycles of its period.

source.archive: MAST (Barbara A. Mikulski Archive for Space Telescopes)

citations.text: TESS Light Curves - All Sectors, STScI/MAST

steps: Read TIME, PDCSAP_FLUX, PDCSAP_FLUX_ERR and QUALITY from the LIGHTCURVE binary table.
Keep cadences with QUALITY 0 and a finite time, flux and error.
Divide flux and error by the median kept flux.
Average into 60-minute bins from t0, keeping bins with at least 3 cadences.
Store time, flux and error as table-columns/1.

assumptions: PDCSAP flux has had instrumental systematics and crowding removed by SPOC; that correction is used as published.
Times are barycentric dynamical time for the target, as SPOC corrects them.
The light is the TESS band, not V or I; the run is short, so the period from it is good to a few tenths of a percent and no better.

validation.check: a period search and a six-harmonic refinement find the published period within 2 percent
